text:
Maya Chen: Hey team — ACME Finance just sent the SIG back, asking for question-by-question evidence. Starting with Q12 (encryption in transit) and Q19 (KMS key lifecycle). Can we assemble screenshots + config snippets? Need to return by EOD PST.

Raj Patel: On it. Do we have a canonical screenshot for TLS termination? I can take from prod load balancer.

Lin Gomez: For Q12: yes, we terminate TLS at the edge and between services we use mTLS. Evidence we typically supply: LB listener config + service mesh mTLS policy screenshot + HTTPS cert metadata.

Tom Alvarez: I can pull the LB listener config and a cert fingerprint. Will paste here once grabbed.

Maya Chen: Perfect. The SIG spreadsheet row is 12 and asks for an "evidence_url" — pls drop a GDrive link. Also Q19 requires KMS key rotation policy and an audit log extract that shows automated rotation ran in last 90 days.

Raj Patel: For KMS, we have two variants depending on customer: managed KMS (cloud KMS) or customer-managed in VPC. Which does ACME want?

Maya Chen: They asked about "customer control of keys" and whether we support BYOK. So both: confirm BYOK + provide sample KMS policy and the onboarding doc.

Lin Gomez: I'll export a redacted KMS key policy and a screenshot from our KMS console showing rotation enabled. Also will attach the key policy JSON and the internal runbook link. For audit logs, Tom — can you produce a 7-day extract showing rotation event? Prefer CSV.

Tom Alvarez: Running a query now:
```
# example: export rotation events
gcloud logging read "resource.type=cloud_kms_crypto_key AND protoPayload.methodName:rotate" --freshness=7d --format csv > kms-rotations.csv
```
Will scrub ARNs and upload to GDrive.

Maya Chen: Awesome. Two quick asks from the SIG reviewer: 1) a screenshot of the key's "rotation schedule" UI; 2) a short one-paragraph statement we can paste: "Redwood supports customer-managed keys (BYOK) with automated rotation..." — can someone draft?

Raj Patel: Draft below — feel free to edit: "Redwood supports customer-managed encryption keys (BYOK) via integration with customer KMS providers (Cloud KMS, AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault). Customers can provision keys in their account and configure Redwood to use those keys for data-at-rest encryption. Rotation can be configured to be automatic or customer-triggered; rotation events are logged to audit logs and available for export."

Lin Gomez: Minor tweak: mention HSM/KMS binding and that our private deployment can use customer HSM via HSM proxy. New draft: "Redwood supports customer-managed encryption keys (BYOK) via Cloud KMS, AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and HSM integrations for Private deployments. Customers can provision keys and restrict access via IAM; Redwood uses these keys for disk and object encryption. Rotation can be automatic or manual; rotation events are logged and available in audit exports."

Maya Chen: Nice. I'll paste that into the SIG response. Can you each drop your artifacts here as GDrive links? Tagging infra-bot to upload the sanitized artifacts once Tom finishes. :pray:

infra-bot: Uploaded files to https://drive.redwood.internal/sig/acme-1918/ — contains: lb-listener.png, mTLS-policy.png, kms-policy.json (redacted), kms-rotation-screenshot.png, kms-rotations.csv (scrubbed), runbook-kms-onboarding.md

Tom Alvarez: Confirmed upload. kms-rotations.csv contains timestamp, key_id (redacted), event_type (rotation), actor (system) — cleaned.

Raj Patel: I added an extra artifact: sample IAM doc showing least-privilege role for redispatcher. Link in the drive folder.

Maya Chen: This is great — I'll attach the drive folder link to the SIG spreadsheet and push the response. If the reviewer asks for signed SLA language or HSM vendor support matrix, ping me and Lin.

Lin Gomez: Also note: for Hosted customers we don't hold customer KMS keys by default; we have a clear BYOK onboarding flow in the runbook. For Private, we can do HSM proxy.

Maya Chen: Closing loop — sending now. Thanks team! :tada:
